## P618: Posterior spinal fusion and instrumentation of the adjacent
vertebrae fracture in an elderly female patient following spinal fusion
surgery using a computer - Assisted rod bending system: a case
report

Teck Siang Lim

1

, Shangeetha Tarmalinggam

1

, Fadzrul Abbas Mohamed Ramlee

1

, Mohd Hezery Harun

1

, Chor Ngee Tan

2

, and Kung Lung Tiong

2

1

Orthopedic, Hospital Pengajar Universiti Putra Malaysia, Serdang,
Malaysia

2

Orthopedic, Hospital Putrajaya, Putrajaya, Malaysia

Introduction: Adjacent segment disease is highly seen in
postoperative patients due to its increased rigidity over the mobile segment
next to a spinal fusion. Common complications reported following a lumbar or
lumbosacral spinal fusion surgery includes disc degeneration, listhesis,
instability, hypertrophic facet joint, arthritis, herniated nucleus pulposus
and stenosis. However, vertebrae spinal fractures are not commonly seen in
spinal fusion surgery, exception of cases in post-menopausal women.
Case Report: 80 years old Chinese lady, known case of
adenocarcinoma of the gallbladder which was diagnosed in 2020, and
laparotomy cholecystectomy was done. Patient was referred to the Orthopaedic
department at Hospital Putrajaya for L1 osteoporotic vertebrae fracture
following posterior spinal instrumentation and fusion. She was initially
presented to a private centre in early 2022 for L3 osteoporotic vertebrae
fracture. Patient was treated with Posterior Spinal Instrumentation and
Fusion (PSIF) L2-S1 and decompression. Post operatively, the patient’s
symptoms resolved and was subsequently discharged home. However, one-month
after the fusion surgery she had a trivial fall at home in sitting position.
Post trauma she was complaining of localized pain over her upper back. There
was a significant tenderness over the L1 region. Bilateral lower limb
myotome and dermatome was preserved. Reflex and tone were normal.
Lumbosacral x-ray revealed adjacent vertebrae compression fracture at L1.
MRI scan of the lumbosacral revealed L1 compression fracture with diffuse
disc bulge causing stenosis over the spinal canal and neural foramen at
L1/L2. Patient was planned for extension Posterior spinal instrumentation
and fusion using computer assisted bending system under general anaesthesia.
Longitudinal midline skin incision made from T9 to S1 to remove the old
rods. Fenestrated percutaneous pedicle screws inserted over T10, T11 and T12
vertebrae with the guidance of C-arm and augmentation done. Rod bending was
done using a computer assisted rod bending system. Pre-bend rods was
inserted connecting the pedicle screws from T10 to S1. Rods tightened and
crosslink inserted. Discussion: There is a high risk of
kyphotic collapse in elderly patients with severe osteoporotic vertebrae
fracture in view of diminished back muscle power to maintain the spinal
alignment. Failure of conservative treatment and unresolve symptoms such as
pain generally directed to surgical intervention. The biggest challenges
faced during the fixation of osteoporotic vertebrae fracture is screw pull
out. The cement augmented pedicle screws also aimed to provide better
stability. In long segment spinal fixation, approximation of the length of
the rod with adequate rod contouring is very difficult. Bending of the rod
using the computer assisted technique rod curves perfectly matches each
screw head where there will be accurate placement decrease the shear of the
screw-bone interface. This computer assisted system also compatible to use
with other system. Conclusion: Computer assisted rod bending
system in posterior spinal fusion and instrumentation surgery with
fenestrated screw in an osteoporotic vertebra is an effective approach to
achieve adequate spinal stability, especially in long segment spinal
fixation during revision surgery. It also marked reduce the shear force at
the pedicle screw bone interface.

Introduction: To evaluate the surgical indications,

of a series of 16 cases of complex neglected sacral fractures treated using
bilateral spinopelvic fixation (BSF) or triangular osteosynthesis (TO) in a
traumatology and orthopedics referral center. Material and
Methods: Longitudinal study, based on a retrospective review of
medical records of patients with complex sacral fractures admitted between
2014 and 2020. All patients older than 18 years and whose time of evolution
between trauma and the surgical procedure was equal or greater than three
weeks were included. Results: The mean age was 39.8 years (18
to 71 years). Anterior pelvic ring injuries represented the most common
association, present in 12 (75%) cases. In 8 (50%) cases there was no
neurological injury, 1 (6.2%) individual evolved with paresthesia, 2 (12.5%)
with paresis in the lower limbs and 5 (31.3%) with sphincter dysfunctions.
Among the patients with neurological impairment, 4 (50%) evolved with
complete improvement, 2 (25%) showed partial improvement and 2 (25%) cases
remained with the deficit. The mean surgical time was 3.6 hours for TO and
4.9 hours for BSF. Postoperative complications occurred in 4 (44.4%)
patients who underwent BSF and there were no postoperative complications in
the TO group. The minimum follow-up was 18 months and all the individuals
analyzed showed good evolution. Conclusion: The surgical
management of neglected complex sacral fractures using TO and BSF proved to
be safe and effective. Indirect or direct decompression, even in neglected
injuries point to an improvement in the neurological status.

## P620: Traumatic spinal injury patterns of on vs. off-road motorcycle

Introduction: Two-wheel motorized vehicles used in both street

spinal injury patterns among these motorcycle injury patients in the US. The

## P621: A retrospective analysis of concomitant spinal injuries in the
setting of polytrauma at a tertiary hospital in Singapore

Theophilus Qiu

1

, Cassie Yang

2

, Shermane Lim

1

, and Zhi Xu Ng

3

1

Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, Medical Student, National
University of Singapore, Singapore, Singapore

2

Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Singapore General Hospital,
Singapore, Singapore

3

Department of General Surgery, Khoo Teck Puat Hospital, Singapore,
Singapore

Introduction: Polytrauma involving multiple organ systems is a
pertinent health concern. In particular, traumatic spinal injuries are often
observed in polytrauma, with serious consequences to patients’ quality of
life and significant healthcare burden. Due to its complexity, there are
limited studies analysing the population of spinal injuries in polytrauma in
Singapore. This study aims to retrospectively evaluate a cohort of
polytrauma patients and characterise the relationship between the presence
of traumatic spinal injury and clinical outcomes. Material and
Methods: A retrospective cohort of patients who presented to the
emergency department for multi-system trauma was assembled from a local
trauma database at a tertiary hospital in Singapore, from January 2012 to
June 2020. Variables analysed were presence of concomitant spine injury,
mechanism of injury, injury severity score (ISS), gender, age, ethnicity and
year of admission. Outcomes were mortality, length of stay and cost.
Results: 1568 patients involved in multisystemic trauma
were identified for this study. It was observed that 27.2% (n = 427) had
concomitant spinal injuries, of which was most commonly due to falls (83.6%,
n = 357), followed by vehicular accidents (12.9%, n = 55). Percentage of
falls as primary injury mechanism increased from 25.9% in the 21- to
30-years-old age range to 96.4% in the 81- to 90-year-old age range.
Meanwhile, the percentage of vehicular accidents as primary injury mechanism
decreased from 67.8% in the 21- to 30-years-old age range to 3.2% in the 81-
to 90-year-old age range. Notably, the mortality rate of patients with spine
injuries (2.6%, n = 416, relative risk 0.17) was significantly lower than
those without spine involvement (15.1%, n = 969, p < 0.001), with an
adjusted odds ratio for mortality of 0.25 (95%CI [0.11, 0.52], p <
0.001). The mean total length of stay was lower in patients with spinal
injuries 11.8 (14.6, p < 0.001) days (SD) compared to 16.0 (28.0) days in
patients without spinal injuries. Mean total hospital bill was lower in
patients with spinal injuries, at 8692 (13980, p < 0.001) Singapore
Dollars (SD), compared to patients without spinal injuries, at 16359
(30658). Conclusion: Spinal injury in the context of polytrauma
is not an independent predictor of poorer outcomes, as it has been observed
to have lower mortality compared to polytrauma patients without spinal
involvement. This may be attributed to the complex nature of polytrauma;
previous studies have found that high-energy traumatic injuries tend to be
associated with more independent living and mobility than low-energy
injuries, with the former having better functional outcomes post-injury.
Similarly, patients with spinal cord involvement in polytrauma, which
suggests a high-energy injury, may have greater functional demands and
subsequently better reserves, hence conferring better survivability.

## P622: Correlation of neuropathic pain intensity and neurological recovery
in patients with spinal cord traumatic injury

Oleksii Nekhlopochyn

1

, Iaroslav Tsymbaliuk

2

2

, and Milan Vorodi

2

1

Spinal Neurosurgery

2

Restorative Neurosurgery Department, Romodanov Neurosurgery
Institute, Kyiv, Ukraine

Introduction: Neuropathic pain is one of the main secondary
complications of spinal cord injury. The biological role of neuropathic pain
has not been established yet. This type of pain is formed directly in the
area of the spinal cord injury; therefore, it can be assumed that its
intensity can characterize both degenerative and reparative processes. The
aim of this work is to assess the possible relationship between the
intensity of neuropathic pain in patients with spinal cord injury and the
dynamics of neurological disorders regression. Material and
Methods: We performed a retrospective analysis of patients
applied to outpatient department of Romodanov Neurosurgery Institute of
National Academy of Medical Sciences of Ukraine in the period from 2010 to
2020 after surgical treatment of spine traumatic injury. The level of
neurological disorders and the intensity of neuropathic pain were assessed
within 5–7 and 11–13 months after surgery. Results: All 102
patients selected for analysis were divided into three groups depending on
the intensity of the registered pain sensations: 1) absence of constant pain
sensations - 19.6% of victims, 2) moderate pain - 56.9%, 3) severe
neuropathic pain – 23.5%. In the first group, the regression of neurological
disorders was 3.5 (95% confidence interval (CI) 2.15-6.15) points, in the
second - 25.0 (95% CI 24.14-29.58) points, in the third - 13.0 (95% CI
10.87-16.55) points. The differences are statistically significant (χ2 =
60.4, df = 2, p < 0.0001). In patients with severe neurological
disorders, the dynamics of recovery did not correlate with the pain
intensity. With ASIA B patients in group 1 the dynamics was 8.5 (95% CI
-10.56-27.56) points, in group 2 - 15.0 (95% CI 13.41-18.41) points, in the
3rd group - 10.5 (95% CI 7.45-14.89) points. In patients with functional
class ASIA C the difference is even more pronounced: in group 1, the median
was 8.0 (95% CI -0.83-20.83) points, in group 2 - 32.0 (95% CI 25.41-36.86)
points, in the third - 15.5 (95% CI 10.27-27.4) points. With ASIA D, a
similar trend was observed. Conclusion: The worst regression of
neurological disorders is observed in patients without clinically
significant pain, the best results of neurological dysfunction recovery are
in patients with moderate neuropathic pain.

## P623: Clinical and radiological outcome of lumbopelvic fixation in Isler
class II and III unstable sacral fractures

Umair Nadeem

1

1

Department of Orthopedics and Spine Surgery, Ghurki Trust Teaching
Hospital, Lahore, Pakistan

Introduction: Many sacral fractures can be treated
non-operatively. Unstable sacral fractures, usually as part of pelvic ring
injury and those with neurological involvement need surgical fixation.
Iliosacral screws, tension band ilio-iliac plating and transiliac bars can
be used in sacral fractures not compromising the lumbosacral articulation
(Isler I). Fractures entering the L5-S1 facets (Isler II) and those entering
the lumbosacral spinal canal (Isler III) need lumbopelvic fixation for
proper biomechanical stability. Objective is to study the clinical and
radiological outcome of lumbopelvic fixation of Isler II and Isler III
unstable sacral fractures. Material and Methods: It was a
prospective cohort study at Ghurki Trust Teaching Hospital Lahore from Jan
2019 to December 2020. All patients with unstable Isler II and Isler III
sacral fractures were recruited for this study. All patients were submitted
to lumbopelvic fixation using a Posterior Triangular Osteosynthesis (PTO)
construct. Patients were evaluated clinically and radiologically, including
full lumbopelvic X-Rays and 3DCT scan at the pre- and postoperative period.
Clinical parameters included a full neurological examination, VAS, ODI.
Results: A total of 13 patients including 8 males and 5
females with mean age of 26 ± 9.4 years were recruited for this study. All
patients had either unstable sacral fractures, 7 had Isler II and 6 had
Isler III. Sacral fracture was part of a pelvic ring injury complex in 10
patients. Neurology was disturbed in 9 patients. The mean followup period
was 20.1 ± 9.6 months. The mean preoperative VAS improved from 9.2 ± 2.4 to
2.2 ± 1.3 postoperatively, while the mean preoperative ODI improved from
86.5 ± 5.6 to 14.5 ± 5.1 postoperatively. Fracture healing was complete
radiologically in all patients and none needed revision. Residual deformity
was present in 33% of the cases with no clinical import. 2 patients had
superficial SSI who were treated uneventfully with antibiotics.
Conclusion: Lumbopelvic fixation is a useful procedure in
the treatment of unstable Isler II and Isler III sacral fractures with
satisfactory clinical and radiological outcome.

## P624: Hyperbaric oxygenation in complex therapy of spinal cord traumatic

Introduction: Spinal cord traumatic injury as resulting

number of experimental and clinical studies aimed at developing methods for
restoring lost functions, there is no solution to the problem that is
acceptable in terms of efficiency. One of the promising directions in the
treatment and rehabilitation of this category of patients is the use of

neuroprotective effect in spinal cord injury, but the results of clinical
application of the method are still contradictory. Material and

the following factors were considered: gender, age, circumstances of injury,
type of damage to the osteoligamentous apparatus, level of neurological

ratio, adjusted for additional analyzed factors, showed a more pronounced

Conclusion: The obtained results indicate that usage of HBO
as a method of complex therapy for traumatic spinal cord injury is promising

Results: Persistent pain sensations in the period of 12‒18

## P626: Acute cauda equine syndrom induced by subdural lumbar hematoma

Eya Chahed

, Nessrine Nessib

, Nessrine Jemel

, Khalil Ghedira

1

, and Sofiene Bouali

1

1

Neurosurgery, National Institute of Neurology, Tunisia

Although spinal anesthesia is commonly used for many types of surgeries,
subdural lumbar hematoma is one of its rare complications. It is a serious
complication that is favored by the use of anticoagulant.
We, here, present a case of 81 year old man who had a surgery for an inguinal
hernia which was complicated by a scrotal hematoma for which he was operated
under spinal anesthesia. He had a history of persistent atrial fibrillation
and was on anticoagulants.
A day later, he developed lower limb paresthesia and motor deficit as well as
retention of urine.
A cerebral and spinal MRI was performed and showed a subarachnoid hemorrhage
and a spinal hematoma from D12 to L5.
He then underwent emergency surgery which consisted of a spinolaminectomy of
L1-1-3 extended to L4 in order to evacuate the compressive intra dural
hematoma.
He had not recovered from his deficit afterwards.
So although this complication is extremely rare, we as neurosurgeons and
physician in general, must keep in mind that it is a possible complication
of spinal anesthesia.

## P627: Percutaneous transpedicular cervicothoracic fixation guided by 2D
fluoroscopy

Joao Oliveira

1

, Sara Sequeira

1

, and Ding Zhang

1

1

Neurocirurgia, Centro Hospitalar Lisboa Ocidental, Lisboa,
Portugal

Introduction: Subaxial cervical transpedicular fixation confers
a biomechanical advantage when compared to instrumentation to lateral
masses. However, it is a challenging technique due to the pedicles small
size and marked convergency, as well as the verterbral arteries close
proximity which leads to an increased risk of neurovascular complications.
Material and Methods: We present a clinical case of a C7-T1
fracture disclocation treated with percutaneous transpedicular fixation and
describe the surgical technique. Results: A 60-year-old-man,
with no relevant medical background, present to our emergency room with
cervical trauma after falling from a bicycle. He had no neurological
deficits. Computed tomography (CT) documented a C7-T1 fracture-dislocation
with grade I/IV anterolisthesis, associated with fracture of the lamina, C7
right pars interarticularis and T1 left pars interarticularis. The patient
underwent urgent surgery, initially with an anterior approach, with open
reduction and C7-T1 arthrodesis with intersomatic cage and plate. Given the
instability caused by a fracture of the pars interarticularis, the patient
underwent a second intervention, seven days later, through a posterior
approach with percutaneous transpedicular fixation of C7-D1 guided by 2D
fluoroscopy (C-arm). In a Concorde positioning, with the skull fixed with a
Mayfield, and pre-operation insurance of a good-quality views in the
anteroposterior, lateral and oblique planes. This last view is essential for
the proper positioning of the transpedicular screws, and the C-arm rotation
was established according to the preoperative study of the convergence angle
of the pedicles to introduce the percutaneous cannula. The percutaneous
entry point was established in the oblique view, after obtaining a perfectly
circular shape of the pedicle contour, and the incision was made at the
point of projection on the skin in the center of this circle. The four
pedicles were progressively cannulated under fluoroscopic support,
alternating between orthogonal and oblique views. The remaining percutaneous
instrumentation technique was the usual. There were no complications and the
control CT showed adequate positioning of the instrumentation and the
patient was discharged 72 hours after the operation, without neurological
deficits. Conclusion: Placement of subaxial cervical
transpedicular screws at the cervicothoracic junction is challenging, due to
its anatomical features and risk of significant neurovascular injury. In C7,
the vascular risk is lower due to the usual absence the vertebral artery at
this level, and the pedicle usually assumeslarger dimensions. With proper
preoperative planning and intraoperative imaging support, it is possible to
safely place transpedicular screws in this anatomical region. Minimally
invasive percutaneous approach allows for faster recovery and shorter
hospital stay.

## P628: Extended cervical pneumorrachis due to closed head injury: report
of two cases and literature review

Zohra Souei

1

, Mohamed Boukhit

1

, Maher Hadhri

1

, Chiheb Abdelileh

1

, Ghassen Belkahla

1

, Kais Maamri

1

, and Mehdi Darmoul

1

1

Neurosurgery, Fattouma Bourguiba University Hospital, Monastir,
Tunisia

Introduction: Pneumorrachis (PR) is defined by the presence of
air in the spinal canal. Rarely reported, it can be secondary to
degenerative, infectious, tumoral, or iatrogenic pathologies and is
exceptionally caused by head trauma. Material and Methods: We
report two cases of polytrauma patients with PR and discuss the causes,
mechanisms, and implications of this condition. Furthermore, a literature
review was carried out. Results: In these 2 cases, PR was
accidentally found during CT diagnostics and remained asymptomatic. One

alarm the attending physician to look for other associated lesions,
particularly the possibility of a CSF leak, which may require intervention.
Conclusion: Pneumorrachis is a rare entity and has a wide
variety of etiologies. Rarely causing neurological symptoms, its presence is
often diagnosed by CT, which is very effective in detecting PR and
specifying its extent and starting point in order to discuss the adequate
treatment.

## P629: Our experience of damage control principle of acute spinal cord
injury in polytraumatized patients

Oleksii Nekhlopochyn

1

 and Yurii Pedachenko

2

1

Spinal Neurosurgery

2

Department of Miniinvasive and Laser Spinal Neurosurgery, Romodanov
Neurosurgery Institute, Kyiv, Ukraine

Introduction: The last few decades are characterized by a
significant change in the structure and nature of traumatic injuries in the
adult population with a pronounced tendency to increase high-energy damage.
The progressive increase in the number of road traffic accidents, natural
and man-made disasters, industrial injuries and the active development of
military conflicts leads to the fact that polytrauma is the leading cause of
death for the young and most active population. The purpose of our study was
to analyze the effectiveness of a two-stage Damage Control surgery in
treatment of spinal cord injury in patients with severe polytrauma.
Material and Methods: We have performed a retrospective
analysis of 75 patients therapy results. All patients had Injury Severity
Score > 17, neurological disorders ASIA A-C and unstable fracture or
fracture-dislocation regardless of injury level. Patients were divided into
3 groups depending on the timing and extent of surgical treatment: first
group – patients, whose surgical treatment was delayed until the relative
stabilization of somatic status, therapy was carried out on the principle of
“too sick to operate on”; second group - patients initially hospitalized in
a specialized center, whose assistance was provided timely and totally -
“Early total care” group; and the third group of patients - neurosurgical
care was carried out in stages, in accordance with the principles of Damage
Control. Neurological disorders regression, mortality and duration of
intensive therapy were analyzed. Results: Patients with delayed
surgery demonstrate the worst recovery rates of neurological deficits. Early
one-stage decompression-fusion surgery ensures better regression of
neurological disorders, but is characterized by a sufficiently high level of
mortality and duration of intensive therapy. The group of patients who
underwent staged surgical treatment is characterized with the best values of
the analyzed parameters. Conclusion: Damage Control approach
provides the best results in therapy for spinal cord injuries in patients
with polytrauma.

## P630: Development and validation of method to asses traumatic compression

Oleksii Nekhlopochyn

, Ievgenii Slynko

, and Yurii Derkach

Introduction: Mechanical compression of spinal canal resulted
with spine traumatic injury is the fundamental criteria in determining
treatment tactics and prognosis of neurological disorders regression.
Analysis of the literature data demonstrates the absence of a criterion that
allows us to characterize a morphologically heterogeneous substrate that
causes compression of the spinal cord. The purpose of our study was to
formulate a definition, develop and perform a validation of radiologic
criteria for assessing the sagittal size of the morphologically heterogenic
ventrally located traumatic substrates of spinal canal. Material and
Methods: Literature analysis revealed the existing indices and
methods for measuring the value of spinal canal compression, as well as the
clinical significance of the nature and value of compression of the spinal
cord with a traumatic substrate. For the initial verification of the
reliability of the method for assessing a ventrally located traumatic
substrate, a retrospective analysis of neuroimaging data of 150 patients
with traumatic changes in the cervical spine was performed. The data of
X-ray films, computer and magnetic resonance tomograms was analyzed. The
measurements were carried out by three independent experts.
Results: The definition of compressing factor has been
developed, that implies a collective concept and reflects the general
characteristics of pathological anatomical substrates caused by damage to
the vertebral motion segment, leading to deformation of the walls of the
spinal canal and, as a result, causing compression of the structures of the
spinal canal. For quantitative characterization, the sagittal size of the
compressing factor was measured, having an absolute metric value and
characterizing the relative degree of substrate displacement into the spinal
canal. The results obtained by statistical processing reveal high
reproducibility of the measurements. The concordance coefficient was 0.85 at
p = 0.00025. Conclusion: The presented radiographic criteria
should be used for the general characteristics of the clinical case, as well
as for statistical data processing in order to unify the idea of the degree
of spinal canal compression.

## 1965

## P631: "Spinopelvic dissociation" revisiting an ambiguous term: a
systematic review

Ahmed Hassan

1

1

Orthopedics and Trauma Surgery, Faculty of Medicine, Assiut
University, Assiut, Egypt

Introduction: The term Spinopelvic Dissociation or jumper`s or
Suicidal fracture was initially defined in the 1960`s refers to “the
presence of bilateral vertical sacral fracture lines associated with a
transverse fracture line” leading to total separation between the axial
skeleton and the pelvis. However, by time, more classifications were
developed, and more sacral fractures patterns were described in the
literature adding to the complexity of the term. Additionally, over the past
couple of years, more light was shed on the spine-pelvis relation, which
makes restricting the term to this fracture pattern unjustified and out of
date. Material and Methods: A systematic review was conducted
within the framework of the Cochrane Back and Neck Group and reported
according to PRISMA guidelines. All types of study designs were included in
the systematic review. We included studies on sacral fractures in skeletally
mature patients (older than 18 years old) where at least one definition of
the term spinopelvic dissociation was reported. Additionally, studies on
pathological fractures and non-English articles were excluded. Two reviewers
independently performed the screening and selection against the inclusion
and exclusion criteria. The initial screening involved screening the titles
and abstracts of the identified articles. In case of disagreement between
the two reviewers, the article was included for the full text assessment.
The full texts were obtained and assessed and in case of disagreement
between the two reviewers during the full-text assessment, the article was
assessed by a senior reviewer who made the final decision. The search
strategy included both electronic searches and backward and forward
snowballing of the finally included articles to retrieve as many relevant
studies as possible. The electronic searches were conducted on two
databases: PubMed and Scopus libraries using both controlled vocabularies
and free text forms. Search was conducted from the date of database
inception till 1/9/2022. Risk of bias (ROB) of the included studies was
assessed using the JBI ROB assessment tool. Results: Our
initial search yielded 108 deduplicated articles. Then after further
exclusion by the titles and abstracts and later on by full text reading 67
articles meeting the inclusion and exclusion criteria were finally included
for inclusion in the study. Regarding the definition included in the finally
selected articles, although most of them refer to the original definition
and still use the same term “Spinopelvic dissociation”, most of them
describe other fracture patterns beside the original pattern regardless of
the classification system used. This in turn makes the use of the original
term in-applicable. Conclusion: As a result of the
heterogeneity and inconsistency encountered in describing these complex and
rare fracture pattern, we suggest that the term “Spinopelvic dissociation”
should be replaced with a broader term “Traumatic Spinopelvic Instability”.
This term will encompass all complete vertical sacral fracture patterns
whether unilateral or bilateral, passing medial or lateral to the L5-S1
facet joint.

## P632: Patient related factors are the best predicting tool for the

Anton Denisov

Mechnikov I.I, Saint-Petersburg, Russian Federation

Introduction: Oncologic treatments increase the incidence of
spinal metastases. Surgical treatment of spinal metastases results in a high
complication rate, which must set against the expected benefits. Frequently
the factors related with the surgery are propense to get more emphasis in
orthopedic treatment studies of bone oncology. However, in clinical trials
and others oncological studies primary tumor related factors are considered
ones that play an important role in patient overall survival. The aim of
this study was to compare and reveal the best predicting Cox-model for
overall survival using an extended database of patients with spinal
metastases. Material and Methods: The clinical data of 361
patients undergoing surgical management of metastatic spinal tumors were
collected at three tertiary hospitals over two decades. Stratification of
this cohort according to disease, patient and surgery specific
characteristics allowed for univariate and multivariate statistical analyses
(three groups) of study population. Observed overall survival estimates were
calculated by the Kaplan-Meier method. Variables that were statistically
significant in the univariate Cox analysis were fitted in the multivariate
Cox proportional hazard (PH) model. All factors were grouped in relation
with their etiology (surgery, patient, tumor). The independence of
covariates was estimated with Matthews correlation coefficient. Predictors
with coefficient less than 0.40 were considered independents. Verification
of the proportional hazards were assessed with Schoenfeld residuals and
log(-log) survival curves. The Likelihood Ratio Test and the minor Bayesian
information criterion were used for selection of the best model. A
two-tailed probability (p) value of < 0.1 was considered for selection
from the univariate to multivariant Cox PH regression. The statistical
difference (p-value) was set at < 0.05 for multivariate Cox PH
regression. Results: A total of 361 patients were included in
the present study with median follow-up of 13 months. At the latest
follow-up, a total of 272 patients (75%) had died. The 3-, 6-, 12-, and
24-month overall survival (OS) rates were 86.7%, 78.4%, 57.1% and 34.7%. The
risk factors included severe grade of CCI, rapid Katagiri tumor type,
presence of lung metastasis, non-ambulatory status at follow-up. The
protective factors were metastasectomy, and postoperative systemic therapy.
Cox-Shell residuals analysis revealed that the best precise and predictive
model is one which includes only patient related factors (CCI, ambulatory
follow-up). Conclusion: For the prediction of the overall
survival of the patients underwent oncological operation due spinal
metastasis more convenient the usage Charlson Comorbidity Index and
ambulatory follow-up status.

## P633: Fully endoscopic spine separation surgery in metastatic disease -
technical note and early results

Kajetan Latka

1

, Dariusz Latka

1

, Waldemar Kolodziej

, Jacek Chowaniec

1

, Tomasz Olbrycht

1

, and Tomasz Sobolewski

1

1

Neurosurgery, Institute of Medicine, University of Opole, Opole,
Poland

Introduction: The purpose of this report is to describe the
surgical methodology and potential effectiveness of endoscopic separation
surgery (ESS) in patients with metastatic spine disease. This concept may
reduce the invasiveness of the procedure, which can potentially speed up the
wound healing process and thus the possibility of faster application of
radiotherapy. Material and Methods: In this study, the
separation surgery for preparing patients to radiotherapy was performed with
fully endoscopic spine surgery (FESS) method followed by percutaneous screw
fixation (PSF). Results: Three patients with metastatic spine

application. The technique of using endoscopic access in spine metastatic
patients is extremely difficult, it must be selected individually and well
planned. Further trials are needed to unambiguously determine whether this
is a potentially new method of treating patients or a dead end. Our results
so far only show that this access is possible to make, but whether it will
bring the expected benefits requires a huge number of cases.

## P634: Ossification of the common anterior vertebral ligament: a rare
cause of dysphagia

Ghassen Gader

1

, Kamel Bahri

1

, Mohamed Amine Gharbi

2

, Mouna Rkhami

1

, Skander Guediche

1

, Mohamed Zouaghi

1

, Mohamed Badri

1

, and Ihsen Zammel

1

1

Department of Neurosurgery, Trauma and Burns Center, Ben Arous,
Tunisia

2

Department of Orthopaedics, Mongi Slim Hospital, La Marsa,
Tunisia

Introduction: Ossification of the common anterior vertebral
ligament, more commonly known as Forestier's disease or senile spinal
ankylosing hyperostosis, is a rare rheumatic disease of unknown aetiolog. It
is characterized by ossification of the paraspinal ligaments and peripheral
entheses. Most often asymptomatic, it is usually discovered incidentally on
standard radiographs. Case report: We report the case of a
65-year-old diabetic patient who presented for gait disturbances and slow
and progressive onset of dysphagia. This dysphagia was improved by flexion
of the neck and worsened by extension, associated with slight
cervicobrachial neuralgia. Esophageal transit revealed an imprint on the
posterior wall of the hypopharynx at the level of C3-C4. Cervical MRI showed
the presence of a bar ossification of the anterior and posterior vertebral
common ligament extending from C2 to C4. The patient was operated through an
anterior approach in order to perform a C4 corporectomy associated to
interbody fusion. Postoperative course was favorable with regression of
dysphagia and motor disorders. Discussion: Forestier's disease
is a generalized joint disorder characterized by ligamentous ossification
and especially of the anterior longitudinal ligament. Several etiological
hypotheses were discussed: mechanical, dietary, metabolic, and environmental
factors. Its incidence increases with age. Ossification along the posterior
vertebral common ligament is also often associated. This disease is most
often asymptomatic and discovered incidentally on imaging. When symptomatic,
the most frequent symptoms are pain, stiffness and reduced mobility of the
affected areas. Complications should be suspected in case of acute symptoms.
The most severe are cervical myelopathies, vertebral fractures and
compressions of adjacent structures. Respiratory signs and swallowing
problems usually improve after surgery. Conclusions:
Forestier's disease is an entity characterized by exuberant bone
proliferation at sites of ligament and tendon insertions with spinal and
extra spinal manifestations. Its diagnosis can be difficult, but the outcome
remains generally favorable.

## P635: Treatment of acute neurological deficit in patients with spinal
metastasis with unknown primary -12 year reterospective review

Rohan Parihar

1

, Samir Dalvie

1

, Kshitij Chaudhary

, R. Dileepan Chakrawarthi

, and Sourav Chatterjee
3

1
Spine Surgery Department, PD Hinduja Hospital, Mahim, Mumbai,
India,
Introduction: Acute neurological deficit in patients presenting
with Metastatic Epidural Spinal Cord Compression (MESCC) requires emergency
spinal cord decompression. The treatment recommendations for MESCC differ
for patients with known metastasis versus those presenting with unknown
primary. Solid organ metastasis with known diagnosis surgery is preferred
while for hematolymphoid malignancies radiotherapy is preferred
respectively. However, this decision cannot be made for patients presenting
to Emergency Room (ER) without a prior cancer diagnosis. We undertook this
study to estimate the incidence of hematolymphoid malignancies presenting as
unknown primary with neurological deficit. Materials and
Methods: Retrospectively reviewed a single hospital database of

2 (11.1%), Thyroid 2 (11.1%) and pancreas 1 (5%). Thoracic spine was the
most common site (15, 83%) followed by lumbar and cervical spine
respectively. Preoperative neurological deficit was Frankel A (5), B (1), C
(8), and D (3). Nine patients (50%) with hematolymphoid malignancy presented

instability. However, in an emergency setting when the diagnosis is not
known quickly enough, surgery has to be offered despite the knowledge that
about 50% of patients will have histology that is ultra-radiosensitive. At
present, there is no reliable way to establish a histopathological diagnosis
in the emergency setting.

## P636: Preservation of neurological function justified anterior corpectomy
with reconstruction in treating patients of thoracolumbar spinal metastatic
tumors

Chien-JenHsu

1

1

Department of Orthopaedics, Kaohsiung Veterans General Hospital,
Kaohsiung, Taiwan

Introduction: The choices of managements are controversial for
metastatic tumor of thoracolumbar spine due to the diversity of patient
condition and un-predictable prognoses. We intended to investigate outcomes
of anterior corpectomy with reconstruction for metastatic tumor of
thoracolumbar spine. Material and Methods: This study
registered 27 cancer patients with thoracolumbar spinal metastases
undergoing anterior corpectomy with reconstruction combining posterior
instrumentation form Jan 2010 to Dec 2019. The origins of malignancy were 13
lung carcinoma, 8 breast carcinoma, 4 renal cell carcinoma, 1 colon
carcinoma, and 1 malignant lymphoma. By using the neurologic, oncologic,
mechanical, and systemic (NOMS) decision framework, The main surgical
indication was determined as intractable back pain or sciatica with
myelopathy that pre-operative MRI demonstrated significant compression on
spinal cord. In addition to posterior transpedicular instrumentation,
adequate decompression was achieved by removing the tumor mass through
anterior corpectomy. For tumors with high vascularity in 4 patients,
pre-operative embolization was performed to decrease blood loss and
operative risk. In the meanwhile, vertebral reconstruction by mesh cages
containing autogenous ribs or allogenous bone graft was conducted. Same day
operations were done if the neurological symptoms were progressing.
Otherwise, posterior instrumentation followed by anterior procedure were
performed on separate days to avoid potential complications of extended
operative time. The postoperative follow-up was arranged every 2 weeks after
discharge from hospital in the first month, thereafter the regular follow-up
was advised at 3 months interval. Results: No surgical
complications required further surgical management in all patients. The
average hospital days were 24 days. Except 3 patients remaining Frankel A as
pre-operative status, the other patients achieved at least one Frankel grade
improvement and relief of back pain. The mean survival time was 16 months
with SF-36 questionnaire improvement from 52 to 80 postoperatively. No
neurological deficit of both lower extremities developed at their last
visits at outpatient clinic or before their mortalities. Neither
dislodgement of mesh cage nor screw loosening was disclosed on follow-up
radiographs at last outpatient visit. No re-hospitalization was caused by
operation-related situation during follow-up except hospice care.
Conclusion: Tumor excision by anterior vertebrectomy
eliminates the compression on spinal cord directly. Motor and sensory
function of lower extremities were therefore preserved. Meanwhile, back pain
and sciatica were relieved by posterior instrumentation. However, patients
with evident progression of muscle weakness pre-operatively could not
achieve neurological recovery. The vertebral reconstruction after
vertebrectomy provided anterior support to achieve at least a mid-term
effect of construct stability. Consequently, the patients regained
symptom-free lives before their mortalities. Even the life expectancy cannot
be extended, posterior instrumentation and anterior vertebrectomy with
reconstruction improved the life quality for cancer patients with spinal
metastasis. Considering preservation of neurological function, anterior
corpectomy deserves a recommendation for patients of thoracolumbar spinal
metastatic tumor with incomplete neurological deficit.

## P637: Surgical management of spinal metastases of the thoracolumbar
junction.

Vanessa Hubertus

1

, Michelle Marino

1,2

, Charlotte Buhre

1

, Peter Vajkoczy

1

, and Julia Onken

1

1

Neurosurgery, Charité Universitätsmedizin Berlin and Berlin
Institute of Health, Berlin, Germany

2

Neurosurgery, Vivantes Klinikum am Friedrichshain, Berlin,
Germany

Introduction: Spinal metastases of the thoracolumbar junction
(TLJ) are common and pose a challenge for treatment due to the region`s
anatomy and associated high rates of neurological deficits and postoperative
complications. The aim of our study is to compare surgical strategies for
TLJ metastases (Th11-L1) with respect to complexity and associated
complications. Material and Methods: 100 patients were treated
surgically due to TLJ metastases in 2005-2020 at a tertiary neurosurgical
care center. Patients receiving only kyphoplasty (n = 11) were excluded from
this study. Spinal instability neoplastic score (SINS), clinical, surgical
and outcome data were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were divided into 3
surgical groups: Decompression only (i), decompression and instrumentation
(ii) and decompression and instrumentation with corpectomy (iii).
Results: 27 patients were decompressed (30%), 48 patients
were treated with decompression and instrumentation (54%), and 14 patients
received decompression and instrumentation combined with corpectomy (16%).
In the median 5 vertebrae were instrumented in groups ii and iii, however
with greatly varying range (3-9). Median SINS was 10 (i), 12 (ii) and 13
(iii). Preoperative neurological deficits were most common in patients
treated with decompression (57%) and instrumentation (37%), whilst no
deficits occurred in patients treated with corpectomy. Mechanical pain was
common in all patients, but higher in patients treated with fusion (ii, iii
88-91% vs. i 61%). Mean duration of surgery was significantly shorter in
group i (149min) compared to group ii (204min) and iii (189min). Surgical
complications occurred in 14% (i), 4% (ii), and 19% (iii), mostly as
surgical site infections. Mortality associated with surgery was 0% and
postoperative survival did not differ significantly between surgical groups.
No secondary Hardware failure (HwF) occurred at a median follow-up of 5-12
months independent of the number of fused segments. Conclusion:
In this cohort, patients with TLJ metastases received instrumentation +/-
corpectomy in case of a potentially unstable and unstable SINS and presented
with a higher rate of preoperative mechanical pain than patients treated
with decompression alone. Surgical complication rate was moderate in all
groups, and dependent on surgical complexity. Postoperative survival did not
differ dependent on surgical complexity. With the instrumentation of in a
median 5 vertebrae, no HwF occurred at a median follow-up of 5-12 months.
Larger patient cohorts are necessary to define the actual number of segments
that need to be instrumented to avoid HwF in metastases of the TLJ.

## P638: Primary spinal canal tumors treated in a tertiary level hopsital in
Nepal - A case series

Rohit Pokharel

1

 and Sushil Paudel

1

1

Dept. of Orthopaedics and Trauma Surgery (Spine Unit), Institute of
Medicine, Maharajgunj Medical Campus, Kathmandu, Nepal

Background and Purpose: Primary spinal tumors are rare
neoplastic lesions. Its incidence varies among the reports because of
difference in sample size and classification of the tumors. Irrespective of
its type, the common presentation are features of space occupying lesion;
distal neurological deficits, back pain and radicular pain. High index of
suspicion and interpretation of relevant investigations are key for reach to
diagnosis. The purpose of the study was to find out relative frequency of
various primary spinal tumors presenting to our hospital, their management
and outcomes. Materials and Methods: This is a retrospective
study done at the Department of Orthopaedics and Trauma surgery (Spine
Unit), Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, Nepal over a period of 11
years from January 2010 to December 2020. All primary spinal tumor cases
(with neurological deficits) operated and have histopathological report are
included in the study. Primary bony tumors of the spine are excluded.
Results: A total of 76 patients with primary spinal tumor
arising in the spinal canal encroaching the neural tissues were operated.
The patient’s age ranged from 7 to 65 years with a mean of 49.5 years; there
was slight male predominance (male female ratio of 42:34 = 1.2:1).
Anatomical location of the tumors was; cervical -6, thoracic- 29,
throcolumbar- 21 and lumbo-sacral- 20. There were 3 (3.9%) primary spinal
extradural lymphomas. Majority, 62 (81.6%) were intradural extramedullary
(IDEM); 30 Schwanoma, 18 meningioma, 9 neurofibroma, 3 dermoid cysts, 1
lipoma and 1 primary mesenchymal chondrosarcoma. Seven (9.2%) were inradural
intrameduallry; 5 (6.6%) were muxopapillary ependymomas and 2 astrocytoma;
and 4 were dumbbell tumors (3 neurofibroma and 1 Schwannoma). The mean
follow-up was 16 months ranged from 6 weeks to 60 months. All patients
improved both neurologically and functionally after surgery except three.
One elderly with conus medullaris ependymoma did not improve, out of two
cases with anteriorly located Schwannoma at T4-5 level one developed
incomplete neurology and another had complete neurological deficit after the
surgery. One case of Schwannoma and two cases of ependymoma had recurrence
of the tumor after average of 1.8 years of the index surgery and were
re-operated. Conclusion: Primary spinal canal tumors are
uncommon lesions and should be one of the differentials of any spinal
lesions. IDEM tumors are common with highest frequency of Schwannoma
followed by meningioma. Early diagnosis and total excision surgical
intervention has very good result.
Keywords: extradural, Intradural extramedullary tumor, Spinal canal, Surgical
excision

## P639: Review of a series of Ewing sarcoma in a Spanish tertiary
center

Borja Sanz

1

, Marta González Pombo

1

, Irene Iglesias Lozano

1

, José Luis Gil Salú

1

, Álvaro Prada Vega

1

, David Mesa Collantes

1

, Leyton Hernán Catari Mallea

1

, Jesús Riqué Dormido

1

, and Francisco Rodríguez Peña

1

1

Neurosurgery, Hospital Universitario Puerta del Mar, Cádiz,
Spain

Introduction: Ewing's sarcoma (ES) is an infrequent malignancy
(WHO grade 4) mainly occurring in adolescents and young adults. It commonly
involves the dorsal spinal column and manifests as myelopathy. We present
three cases in each segment of the spine. Material and Methods:
We review the literature after the diagnosis and treatment of this tumour.
Results:Case 1. 25-year-old man with
cervical pain and tetraparesis. He went to the emergency department and the
MRI showed an extradural cervical mass that caused compression from C2 to C6
that invaded the lateral mass of C4. A posterior decompression, resection
and fusion was performed and in a second stage the lateral mass of C4 was
resected through an anterior corpectomy. He did not present any worsening
and recovered partially from the tetraparesis. He presents 3/5 in the right
arm and is capable of walking short distances. We initiated
vincristine-doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide-etoposide. 10 months
later the patient has a progression free survival (PFS) and the deficits are
improving. Case 2. 19-year-old woman with dorsal back
pain irradiated to the chest. She also presented paraesthesias from a D7-D8
level. A MRI showed an extradural lesion around D4-D6 with widening of the
foramen of D5-D6 along with intense contrast enhancement. A gross total
resection (GTR) was achieved. We initiated
vincristine-doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide-etoposide. After 14
months the patient remains asymptomatic with a PFS and no deficits.
Case 3. 16-year-old woman with lumbar pain
irradiated to both legs with no neurological symptoms. A MRI showed an
isointense and hyperintense in T2 intradural tumour in L3-L4. GTR was
obtained and the pain improved. We initiated ifosfamide/etoposide. 4 months
later the patient remains asymptomatic with a PFS and no deficits. The three
cases presented a similar anatomopathological study. They described a tumour
positive to CD99, FLI-1 and vimentin immunohistochemical stain. It also
presented fusion of FUS genes and ERG. ES was the most likely diagnosis. ES
is an infrequent malignancy mainly occurring in adolescents and young
adults. The most frequent symptom is pain followed by myelopathy. Back pain
and paraesthesia are secondary to irritation. The most common location is
thoracic followed by lumbar and cervical. The intradural presentation is
more frequent than the extramedular. In MRI is isointense on T1 and
hyperintense on T2, with varying gadolinium enhancement in more than 60%.
Other characteristics are dumbbell shape (24%), foraminal widening (19%),
and erosion (19%). GTR plus chemotherapy or radiotherapy is the preferred
treatment. The radiotherapy consists of a neuroaxis irradiation with 30–60Gy
and the chemotherapy usually used is
vincristine-doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide-etoposide. GTR is a
good prognosis factor because it increases the effectiveness of QT-RT. The
prognosis is thought to be dismal due to local invasion and metastases, with
5-year survival of less than 37.5%. Conclusion: ES must be
suspected in cases of rapidly progressing pathology and young patients.
There are no typical radiological signs. GTR and adjutant treatment with
QT-RT is the gold standard.

## P640: Mini-open vertebroplasty in treating C2 osteolytic lesion

Adnene Benammou

1

, Ahmed Ben Abid

1

, Cherif Kamoun

1

, Balti Walid

1

, Amine Lengliz

1

, Mondher Kooli

1

, and Mohamed Ben Salah

1

1

Orthopedic Surgery Department, Charles Nicolle Hospital, Tunis,
Tunisia

Introduction: Percutaneous vertebroplasty is a well-established
technique in treating multiple painful lesions of the thoracolumbar spine.
It can provide pain relief, bone strengthening and vertebral stabilization.
However, its use in the upper cervical spine is rare due to the difficult
access and multiple potential complications. We report a safer technique
with a mini-open vertebroplasty of a C2 osteolytic lesion. Material
and Methods: A 71-year-old man, with history of neck pain for
which he did not seek medical treatment, sustained a road traffic accident.
He presented to our emergency room. Physical examination revealed only pain
of the right clavicle. No neurological deficit was noted. A full body
Computed Tomography (CT) was conducted due to the violence of the trauma. It
revealed a fracture of the right clavicle and an osteolytic lesion of C2
involving the left half of C2 vertebral body. The fracture of the clavicle
was treated conservatively. The decision for the C2 osteolytic lesion was to
proceed with a mini-open vertebroplasty. Surgery was realized in supine
position with head on horseshoe. Fluoroscopy marking of vertebral levels was
realized. We realized a mini right anterior cervical approach exposing the
edge of C2. We inserted the Jamshidi needle on the lytic region under
fluoroscopic control. Biopsy was taken and addressed to the laboratory. We
injected then the PolyMethyl MethAcrylate (PMMA) using the eggshell
technique with injecting in the posterior part, waiting for the cement to
harden and then proceed to injecting the cement to fill the lesion. We used
the eggshell technique to avoid cement leakage and its possible
complications especially at the level of C2. No extravasation was noted.
Results: Intra and postoperative was uneventful. Pain
relief was immediate after surgery. Visual Analog Scale (VAS) decreased from
8 in preoperative to 2 in postoperative. Postoperative CT-scan showed PMMA
in the body of C2 with no sign of extravasation. The patient was ambulated
and discharged the day next surgery and addressed to a medical department to
establish the etiology of the lesion. At 3 months postoperative, there was a
complete pain relief (VAS = 0). Conclusion: Osteolytic lesions
of C2 are rare. They can cause serious neurovascular complications.
Percutaneous vertebroplasty has shown great result in treating thoracolumbar
spine but can be difficult in upper cervical spine. This technique of
mini-open vertebroplasty can be a safer less demanding technique in treating
osteolytic lesions of C2. It has the advantages of vertebroplasty such as
early pain relief and vertebral stabilization without the risk of the
percutaneous technique in the upper cervical spine which can lead to serious
complications.

## P643: En-bloc resection of a recurrent primary lumbar chondrosarcoma of

Sofia Caldeira Dantas

Conclusion: Primary spinal chondrosarcomas are rare tumors
and their complete resection is technically very challenging. Here a
recurrent chondrosarcoma of L5 was submitted to an en-bloc resection. The
surgical technique and alternative options are further presented and
discussed.

## P646: En-bloc vertevrectomy for the treatment of tumor spine - a case
series of 8 patients

João Soares do Vale

1

, Sara Diniz

1

, Sofia Caldeira Dantas

1

, Pedro Cardoso

2

, António Oliveira

3

, and Ricardo Rodrigues-Pinto

1

1

Spinal Unit (UVM)

2

Musculoskeletal Tumors Group, Department of Orthopaedics, Centro
Hospitalar e Universitário do Porto, Porto, Portugal

3

Department of Orthopaedics, Centro Hospitalar do Porto, Porto,
Portugal

Introduction: En-bloc vertebrectomy, also called spondylectomy,
has become an increasingly widespread procedure used for the treatment of
neoplastic spine lesions. It consists of a resection of the entire tumor and
one of more affected vertebrae with margins. The objective of this surgery
is either cure or localized control of the disease. Material and
Methods: This study was a retrospective case series analysis
conducted in a reference center for the treatment musculoskeletal sarcomas.
The data were obtained from medical reports of patients treated between
January of 2007 and June of 2022. Patients with benign aggressive, primary
malignant spine lesions and spine metastasis who underwent en-bloc
vertebrectomy during the study period was evaluated. Results:
Eight patients (four males and four females) underwent total vertebrectomy.
Their mean age at the time of operation was 47 years (18 to 68). The mean
time of follow-up was 70 months (2 to 144). The diagnosis were
chondrosarcoma, giant cell tumor, angiosarcoma, chordoma, high grade
sarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, leiomyosarcoma and breast cancer metastasis. Type 1
to 6 lesions were treated according to Tomita classification. In seven
patients the tumour was in lumbar spine (L1, L3 and L5) and in one patient
in thoracic spine (T8). In four cases a combined approach was used and in
the other four a posterior approach. In three patients, wide margins were
achieved, and in the other 5 were marginal. Three patients died from their
disease with a mean follow up of 57 months (2 to 144). Three showed no
evidence of disease and two are alive with disease. A 50% complication rate
was observed in this series (infection, hardware failure and neurological
injury). Conclusion: Despite being a technically demanding
surgical procedure with a high rate of complications, en-bloc vertebrectomy
is a good solution when the objective is either cure or localized control of
the disease.
In this series it is possible to confirm the effectiveness of vertebrectomy
to achieve the cure and a good survival rate even in patients in which the
procedure was not curative.

## 1185

## P647: Multi-level kyphoplasty for myeloma of more than 3 vertebral levels
can be safe

Jemma Keefe

1

, Mohamed Abdalla

2

, Mark Nyanzu

2

, Priyanshu Saha

1

, Bisola Ajayi

2

, Jason Bernard

2

, Timothy Bishop

2

, and Darren Lui

2

1

St George's, University of London, London, United Kingdom

2

Department of Complex Neurosurgery, St George's Hospital, London,
United Kingdom

Introduction: Vertebral involvement occurs in approximately 70%
of multiple myeloma cases. Percutaneous kyphoplasty (PKP) has been proven to
improve pain and mitigate spinal deformity in myeloma patients. This can be
performed at both single and multi-vertebral level dependent on vertebral
involvement. Pan-spinal infiltration is not uncommon, affecting
approximately 50% of our patients, emphasising the need for multi-level
kyphoplasty. Original guidelines for kyphoplasty have cautioned against
performing kyphoplasty on more than 3 vertebral levels because of the risk
of multiple mini-pulmonary emboli from cement leakage. This may potentially
be due to the fact that each vertebra can hold approximately 5 to 10cc and
it is essentially the volume of cement rather than the number of vertebrae
which is important. This study aims to determine the safety of PKP for more
than 3 vertebral levels. Material and Methods: This was a
retrospective analysis of 45 multiple myeloma cases (mean age = 64.8 ± 1.57,
25 male/20 female) with vertebral involvement of which management involved
PKP from January 2019 to August 2022. Cases involving more than 3 vertebral
levels (N = 16) were compared to cases involving 3 levels or less (N = 29),
with safety and efficacy of PKP analysed through 30-day mortality and
intra-operative complications. Results: For all cases managed
with PKP there was a 30-day mortality of 7.31%. The 30-day mortality in
cases involving 3 vertebral levels or more (N = 14) was 0.00%, with no
intra-operative complications, whereas the 30-day mortality in cases with
less than 3 levels involved (N = 27) was 11.1%. Comparatively, a similar
cohort of patients with multiple myeloma involving the spine that were
managed conservatively (N = 83) at our centre had a 30-day mortality of
8.43%. Conclusion: In this study PKP performed at more than 3
vertebral levels was shown to be a safe procedure with no evidence of
increased mortality or complications compared to procedures involving less
than 3 vertebral levels. We believe that the volume of cement is more
important than the number of vertebrae operated on. Therefore, in future
patients with pan-spinal involvement may be considered for PKP of more than
3 vertebral levels. Further studies are required to characterise more
accurately the safety and efficacy of this procedure for more than 3
levels.

## P648: Can the SORG machine learning algorithms predict 90-day and 1-year
spinal metastatic disease survival in a rural cohort? An external validation
study

James Hall

1

, Michael Garneau

1

, Harmen Kuijten

2,3

, Olivier Q. Groot

2,3

, Trevor Gulbrandsen

1

, Cassim Igram

1

, Andrew Pugely

1

, Catherine Olinger

1

, and Joseph Schwab

2

1

Orthopedics and Rehabilitation, University of Iowa Hospitals and
Clinics, Iowa City, United States

2

Orthopedic Surgery, Massachusetts General Hospital, Harvard Medical
School, Boston, United States

3

Orthopedic Surgery, University Medical Center Utrecht, Utrecht, The
Netherlands

Introduction: To determine the propriety of invasive surgical
procedures, the Skeletal Oncology Research Group machine learning algorithm
(SORG-MLA) was developed to predict 90-day and 1-year survival in spinal
metastatic disease. However, sub-analysis originally demonstrated decreased
probability of prediction in patients who underwent surgery after 2010.
Although further studies demonstrated good performance of these algorithms,
even after 2010, they were based on a cohort of patients in the same region
and have yet to be validated in a varying population. The purpose of this
study was to externally validate the performance of the SORG-MLA on
predicting 90-day and 1-year survival in spinal metastatic disease in a
cohort of patients located in the rural midwestern United States.
Materials and Methods: A retrospective review of patients
who underwent operative management of spinal metastatic disease at one
academic institution (University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics) was
performed. The criteria for inclusion consisted of patients aged ≥ 18 years,
diagnosis of metastatic disease (solid tumor metastasis, multiple myeloma,
lymphoma) with or without pathologic fracture, and operative management
being performed between 2010 – 2021. Exclusion criteria included spinal
metastasis originating from a primary bone tumor (e.g. sarcoma), and death
record or most recent follow-up unavailable. Baseline characteristics of the
validation cohort were obtained and compared to the developmental cohort.
Input parameters to predict survival included 18 variables including primary
tumor histology, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance
Status Scale, American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) Impairment Scale,
and laboratory values. Discrimination (c-statistic and receiver operating
curve), calibration (calibration slope, intercept, calibration plot, and
observed proportions by predicted risk groups), overall performance (Brier
score), and decision curve analysis were utilized to evaluate the SORG-MLA
in this specific external cohort. Results: Overall, there were
249 patients included in this study. The 90-day and 1-year mortality rates
were 63 (25%) and 134 (54%), respectively. The validation cohort compared to
the developmental cohort had significantly more moderate and rapid growth
primary tumors, more visceral metastasis, and lower pre-operative hemoglobin
levels. The SORG-MLA for 90-day and 1-year survival showed strong
discriminatory ability (AUC 0.85 [95% confidence interval [CI] 0.74-0.94]
and 0.82 [95% CI 0.71-0.91], respectively), Brier score, and decision curve
analysis. The 90-day and 1-year mortality showed almost perfect calibration
demonstrated by a calibration intercept of 0.06 [95% CI -0.09-0.21] and 0.02
[95% CI -0.12-0.16], respectively. Conclusion: This external
validation study demonstrated that the SORG ML algorithm utilized in
predicting 90-day and 1-year survival of patient with spinal metastatic
disease exhibited strong performance in this rural, midwestern United States
cohort. Additional, multi-center studies are needed to further validate
these algorithms in differing populations.

Priyanshu Saha

, Emily Tsang

1

, Zion Hwang

, Bisola Ajayi

, Varinder Singh Alg

, Ursalan Khan

, Mohamed Abdalla

Introduction: Radiofrequency Ablation (RFA) is a novel addition
to the armamentarium of radical oncological treatment utilized with other
surgical techniques. It aids in cytoreduction and potentially utilized
independently to be curative and offer maximum local control. RFA as an
adjunct to separation surgery may be a new technique that may have a

including maintenance of ambulation, continence, neurological symptoms and

only. LR –0% at 6 months (n = 9), 12 months (n = 7) and 24 months (n = 5),
pain was well managed, no infection and mortality – 0% at 6 months (n = 11),
12 months (n = 7) and 24 months (n = 5). The Histopathology analysis of the
biopsy case showed increased local necrosis rates of 70%, indicating
neoplastic control. Conclusions: RFA is promising for OMD
pathway which can potentially deliver radical oncological control. As an
adjunct to SS and SABR, it may offer improved cytoreductive control. The
authors believe they are the first to describe this technique used in
conjunction with SS where we show local recurrence of 0% at 2 years.
Furthermore, in carefully selected cases, RFA ± cement has shown excellent
LC and mortality. However, it is important to acknowledge the limited sample
size in our study.

## P650: Anterior separation surgery to allow for stereotactic ablative
radiotherapy: a novel approach permitting radical oncological treatment of
oligometastatic disease

Priyanshu Saha

1

, Emily Tsang

1

, Zion Hwang

1

, Pawan Minhas

2

, Mohamed Abdalla

2

, Bisola Ajayi

2

, Timothy Bishop

2

, Jason Bernard

2

, and Darren Lui

2

1

St George's University of London, London, United Kingdom

2

Department of Complex Neurosurgery, St George's University Hospitals
NHS Foundation Trust, London, United Kingdom

Introduction: A paradigm shift in the treatment of spinal
metastases has allowed surgeons to deliver curative results utilising
radical oncological treatment opposed to traditionally palliative
decompression for neurological symptom and pain management. In
oligometastatic disease and oligo-progressive disease, the accompaniment of
Stereo tactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) as a primary modality or adjuvant
treatment to surgery has been shown to excellent survival outcomes, lower
morbidities, and better pain management. The novel use of carbon fibre VBR
allows optimal planning of SABR, less reflection and better future
surveillance imaging. Carbon fibre has physical and chemical properties that
includes high heat tolerance, high tensile strength, resistance to corrosion
and conductivity. Carbon fibre reinforced PEEK has mechanical properties
that allow high resistance to ionizing radiation and low wear particles,
which is better suited to the planned SABR as opposed to use of titanium VBR
and screws. Methods/Case: The patient was a 48-year-old lady
with a solitary metachronous lesion in T2, this is a recurrence of her
breast oligometastatic disease in 2014 which was diagnosed and treated in
2014, Spinal Instability Neoplastic Score (SIN) was determined, the location
was junctional (C7-T2), pain free, a lytic bone lesion was found on CT with
normal alignment and no vertebral collapse. The patient also did not present
with any neurological deficit. She was ASA grade 3. She had a Tokuhashi
score of 14 hence indicating she would live more than a year, the revised
Tokuhashi with a Tomita score of 2 indicated for highly morbid excision
surgery. To avoid morbidity, separation surgery with postoperative SABR was
opted. A Bilsky ESCC score of 2 and the Neurologic Oncologic Mechanical and
Systemic framework (NOMS) indicated the patient was suitable for separation
surgery. Although the SIN score was 6 indicating that the patient should not
be operated on and most likely be treated palliatively. separation surgery
was decided for the patient due to the patient’s age and systemic
suitability. This case report illustrates a novel approach to the treatment
of spinal oligometastatic disease utilizing anterior separation surgery with
a custom carbon fibre vertebral body replacement cage followed by
postoperative SABR. Due to several contraindications of posterior separation
surgery and the morbidity associated with radical surgery; anterior surgery
was opted for utilising the philosophy of Enneking radical surgery despite
Enneking inappropriate resection. Results: There were no
complications intraoperatively and post operatively, pain was managed
appropriately in the hospital. Patient did not complain of pain or wasn’t
immobilised outside of the hospital. In both 15 and 30 monthsthe
postoperative follow up MRI and PET CT scans demonstrated that the patient
was tumour-free and the patient was fully mobile, pain free and living
independently. Conclusion: Utilising this novel approach,
Anterior Spinal Separation Surgery and SABR has shown maximum local control
and can deliver curative, radical oncological control without the morbidity
of Enneking radical surgery. The use of carbon fibre VBR has been better
suited for post-operative SABR planning due to the physical properties
superior to titanium.

## P651: Vascular supply and neurological outcome after surgical treatment
of spinal intradural hemangioblastoma: a multicenter retrospective case
series

Vicki Butenschön

1

, Bernhard Meyer

1

, and Maria Wostrack

1

1

Department of Neurosurgery, Technical University Munich, Munich,
Germany

Introduction: Spinal cord hemangioblastoma are rare highly
hypervascularized benign neoplasms. Surgical resection remains the treatment
of choice, with a significant risk of postoperative neurological
deterioration. Methods: Retrospective multicenter study
including five high-volume neurosurgical centers assessing patients
surgically treated for spinal hemangioblastoma between 2006 and 2021.
Clinical status, surgical data, preoperative angiograms, and embolization
were analyzed when available. Follow-up records were reviewed, and logistic
regression performed to assess possible risk factors for neurological
deterioration. Results: We included 60 patients in 5
high-volume neurosurgical centers in Germany and Austria. Preoperative
angiography was performed in 30% of the cases, ten patients underwent
preoperative embolization. The clinical outcome revealed a transient
postoperative neurological deterioration in 38.3%, depending on symptom
duration and preoperative McCormick grading, but patients recovered in most
cases until follow-up. Posterior tumor location and presence of a syrinx
favored gross total tumor resection. Preoperative embolization was not
associated with postoperative worsening. Conclusion: Spinal
hemangioblastoma patients significantly benefit from early surgical
treatment with only transient postoperative deterioration and complete
recovery until follow-up. The performance of preoperative angiograms remains
subject to center disparities.

and Methods: We report the case of a man with solitary

stabilization of L3-L5 is planned. Conclusion: Chordoma is a
rare condition that should be considered in the differential diagnosis of
central destructive lesions in the spine and base of skull. Their management
is not easy.

## P655: Cervical bone metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma: case report

Introduction: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common

secondary localization in C4 of a moderately differentiated carcinoma whose
immunohistochemical phenotype may be consistent with an excreto-biliary
origin which was later confirmed by a liver biopsy. Conclusion:
Bone metastases from HCC are rare; they should, however, be considered in
the presence of any lytic bone lesion, particularly in patients with chronic
liver disease. Given their poor prognosis, their treatment is palliative,
aimed primarily at improving the patient's quality of life.

## P656: Mesenchymal chondrosarcoma of the sacrum : surgical treatment by

Rationale: Chondrosarcoma of the sacrum is a highly unusual

## P657: The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the presentation of patients
with spinal metastases

Aleksander Mika

1

, Colby Wollenman

1

, Anthony Steinle

1

, Hani Chanbour

2

, Wilson Vaughan

1

, Andrew Croft

1

, Julian Lugo-Pico

1

, Scott Lawrence Zuckerman

1,2

, Amir Abtahi

1,2,3

, and Byron Stephens

1,2,3

1

Department of Orthopaedic Surgery

2

Department of Neurological Surgery

3

Center for Musculoskeletal Research, Vanderbilt University Medical
Center, Nashville, TN, United States

Introduction: The COVID-19 pandemic has placed unprecedented
pressure on the US healthcare system, causing a deprioritization of
non-emergency services including elective surgery. Delay in surgical
treatment for oncology patients can result in progression of the disease,
which can complicate surgical care, distort normal anatomy, and worsen
patients ‘preoperative health. Currently, little is known about how the
COVID-19 pandemic has affected preoperative health in patients undergoing
surgical treatment for metastatic disease to the spine. The purpose of this
study was to determine if preoperative Spinal Instability Neoplastic scores
(SINS) and Tokuhashi scores differed in patients receiving surgical care
during the COVID-19 pandemic compared to patients who received surgical care
before the pandemic. Material and Methods: Data was
retrospectively collected from the electronic medical records from a single
institution. All patients who underwent surgical treatment for metastatic
disease to the spine between 3/1/19 to 3/1/21 were included. All cases with
primary spinal tumors or insufficient imaging or chart information were
excluded. Patients were separated into two groups: one group received
surgery between 3/1/19 to 2/29/20 (before COVID restrictions) and the other
group received surgery between 3/1/20 to 3/1/21 (during COVID restrictions).
The following variables were obtained through electronic medical records:
gender, age, race, Bilsky score, cancer type, SINS, Tokuhashi score, and
mortality within 12 months of the index spine surgery. Primary outcomes
included preoperative SINS and Tokuhashi scores. Additionally, patient
postoperative Skeletal Oncology Research Group (SORG) scores were obtained.
Descriptive statistics were performed using Wilcoxon rank-sum test.
Univariate and multivariate linear regression models controlling for age and
cancer histology were performed to determine the association of having a
surgery before or during COVID-19 pandemic with SINS and Tokuhashi scores at
presentation. Results: 52 patients who underwent surgery before
the COVID-19 pandemic were compared to 45 patients who underwent surgery
during the COVID-19 pandemic. There was a significant difference between the
before COVID-19 and during COVID-19 groups with respect to SINS (9.31 ± 2.39
vs 10.84 ± 2.75, p = 0.004) and Tokuhashi scores (9.27 ± 2.35 vs 7.89 ±
2.76, p = 0.009). Linear regression demonstrated that having surgery during
COVID-19 was independently associated with a higher SINS score at
presentation (β = 1.37, 95% CI: 0.32-2.42, p = 0.011) and a lower Tokuhashi
score at presentation (β = -1.45, 95% CI: -2.48-(-0.41), p = 0.006). There
were no differences found between the two groups in 6-week, 90-day, or
1-year SORG scores, nor were there differences between the two groups in
6-month or 1-year mortality rates. Conclusion: The current
study demonstrates that patients undergoing surgical treatment for
metastatic spine disease during the COVID-19 pandemic had significant
differences in SINS and Tokuhashi scores, however, these differences are
likely not clinically significant. This study provides valuable information
regarding the impact the COVID-19 pandemic had on patients receiving
surgical care for metastatic spine disease. While both groups had similar
prognostication scores and 1 year mortality rates, alternative healthcare
delivery modalities, such as telehealth clinic visits, could be an important
tool to help mitigate poor outcomes for this patient population in the
post-COVID era.
